Agreement on Investment of the Framework Agreement on Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Between the People's Republic of China and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ACFTA), signed 3 August 2009

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (2024 revision, effective 1 January 2025); Administrative Measures for Beneficial Owner Information (People's Bank of China and State Administration for Market Regulation Order No. 3 [2024], effective 1 November 2024); Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 revision, effective 1 July 2024); Measures for the Administration of Enterprise Name Registration of the State Administration for Market Regulation; applicable PBOC provisions on customer due diligence and suspicious transaction reporting.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of each direct and ultimate foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or companies registrar of the jurisdiction where the foreign shareholder is incorporated
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel route selection: (A) Apostille Convention member state: notarization or certified true copy by a local notary public, then Apostille by the designated competent authority of that state; stop there and do not add consular legalization. (B) Non-member state: notarization by a local notary, then authentication by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then Consular Legalization by the Embassy or Consulate of the People's Republic of China; stop there and do not add an Apostille. Never chain both paths for the same document.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Existence of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of companies or equivalent corporate registrar in the foreign shareholder's state of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Select only one authentication route based on the issuing state's membership of the Hague Apostille Convention. Route A: local notarization if required, then Apostille. Route B: local notarization, Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication, then PRC Embassy or Consulate legalization. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive for the same instrument and must not be performed in sequence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution authorizing the incorporation of the Chinese WFOE and granting Power of Attorney to the formation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the foreign parent shareholder, certified by the corporate secretary or a notary public of the parent's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The board signatures and resolution must be notarized in the parent's country. If the country is an Apostille Convention member state, attach the competent authority's Apostille and present the bundle to the PRC authorities without consular legalization. If the country is not a member, the same notarized resolution must be authenticated by the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then legalized by the PRC Embassy or Consulate. The two routes are parallel; do not combine them.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Memorandum and Articles of Association of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry, parent company records, or a licensed corporate services provider legally authorized to issue certified copies in the parent's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: A certified true copy of the constitutional documents is taken. Where the issuing state is an Apostille member, apply a single Apostille from the designated competent authority. Where the issuing state is not an Apostille member, use local notarization, Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication, and PRC Consular Legalization. The WFOE filing officer shall ensure only one authentication path is used and shall never present an Apostilled document for consular legalization or vice versa.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter / Lender Good Standing Letter for the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank branch or relationship manager of the foreign shareholder's principal bank in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank letter must be signed by a bank officer whose authority is verified. For Apostille member states, the bank signature is notarized and the document receives a single Apostille; no consular legalization is added. For non-member states, the notarized bank letter is authenticated by the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then consular legalized by the PRC Embassy or Consulate. Both paths remain mutually exclusive and parallel; sequential chaining is prohibited.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before onboarding any shareholder, director, authorized signatory, beneficial owner or bank signatory, the WFOE and its formation agent shall verify each individual and entity against (1) UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions Lists; (2) US OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions lists; (3) PRC Customs Denied Persons and dual-use export control lists; (4) PBOC anti-money laundering suspicious transaction and PEP databases; (5) national credit, bankruptcy, dishonesty and criminal enforcement lists. Screening must be completed no earlier than 24 hours before signing and repeated within 24 hours of any list update. Any high-risk PEP, sanctions hit or unexplained wealth triggers enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds audit, senior management approval, and, if suspicious, a report to CAMLMAC.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation - National Enterprise Registration and Investment System (online enterprise name pre-clearance portal integrated with the nationwide company registration platform)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A WFOE name must be composed in Simplified Chinese characters and must follow the four-tier statutory formula: administrative division + distinctive trade name + industry or business scope expression + legal form suffix (Company Limited / Limited Liability Company). English or romanized names are supplementary and do not replace the approved Chinese name. Phonetic transliteration and pinyin may be used only as a guide to the Chinese characters; the registered legal name is the Chinese character name appearing on the business license. Any English name used in banking documentation, invoices and customs filings must correspond exactly to the approved Chinese legal name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant or its SAMR-licensed formation agent shall obtain the written refusal and rejection code from the enterprise name registration portal. The applicant may then file an administrative reconsideration petition with the State Administration for Market Regulation or its competent local counterpart within 15 days of receipt, stating the proposed name, the refusal code, the factual and legal grounds of the challenge, and the basis in the Company Law and enterprise name registration measures. Alternatively, the applicant may initiate an administrative lawsuit in the competent People's Court within six months of the final reconsideration decision. If the rejection is based on identical or confusingly similar prior rights, the appeal should include a consent letter from the earlier registrant or a revised distinctive token to preserve the 30-day reservation window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a manufacturing WFOE engaged in production of port container gantry cranes and hoisting gear under ISIC 2816, a virtual office or commercial mailbox-only address is not acceptable. The WFOE registered office must be a fixed physical premise leased or owned by the entity, capable of receiving service of process, maintaining statutory books and production, safety or accounting records, and demonstrably serving as the place of actual management. SAMR, municipal tax authorities, customs, industrial safety authorities and banks all reject mailbox-only offices for this industry. A separate engineering or administrative office may be used alongside the production plant, provided both addresses are properly declared, but no registered address may be a mere correspondence drop.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) valid lease certificate or ownership certificate; (2) on-site photographs and GPS coordinates; (3) visible company nameplate; (4) presence of personnel, equipment and records; (5) VAT invoices and utility bills matching the declared address; (6) industrial zoning and environmental permit compliance; (7) safety and fire-control approvals for crane manufacturing. Quantified risk: High, approx. 70-85% likelihood of unannounced physical inspection by SAMR or municipal tax authorities within the first 12 months of WFOE formation. Maintain an actual operating site, keep original statutory books there, and display the business license as legally required.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: SAMR enterprise name pre-clearance and WFOE incorporation registration fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory registration tariff is charged in the PRC for standard company incorporation; official registration is funded through the national consolidated budget.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PRC formation lawyer fees for WFOE structuring, UBO piercing, AML/CFT due diligence and filing support
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Retained PRC-licensed law firm or qualified corporate agency
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a manufacturing WFOE: USD 8,000-20,000 depending on group structure, shareholder jurisdictions and documentary complexity.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, certified translation and authentication of foreign parent corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Local notary public, recognized translation agency and competent certifying authority in the investor's jurisdiction
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market-rate per document and per 100 Chinese characters; provincial notarial fee schedules apply for Chinese-side notarization and translation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or Consular Legalization fees for the documented shareholder instruments
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Designated Apostille competent authority in the origin state or Embassy/Consulate of the People's Republic of China
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Origin-state Apostille fee schedule and PRC consular legalization fee schedule; estimated USD 50-150 per instrument for consular service and USD 10-50 per instrument for Apostille where applicable.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Physical registered office address package for the WFOE (lease deposit, first quarter rent and site survey)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Landlord or property developer; municipal registry evidence fees
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing commercial market rent for an industrial or manufacturing administrative address in the selected city, plus a refundable security deposit of 2-3 months.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Environmental, safety and industrial zoning pre-screening for gantry crane production site
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed environmental consultant and municipal development authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market fee for site eligibility review, environmental classification verification and pre-application advisory report.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Reserve for unforeseen administrative and translation supplements
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Various government service windows and accredited service providers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Contingency reserve of approximately 10% of non-legal regulatory fees to cover additional documentary originals, certification supplements and courier charges.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 revision, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 1-59 (company formation and limited liability company organization), Articles 76-142 (limited liability company governance), and Article 186 (liquidation); Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2020), Articles 6-20; Regulations on Implementing the Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (State Council Order No. 723), Articles 1-21; and the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) Provisions on Company Registration Administration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), acting through local municipal and provincial Market Supervision Administration enterprise registration windows and the National Enterprise Registration Information System.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foreign-Invested Enterprise Establishment Registration Application Form and the Unified Social Credit Code Application Form, submitted through the SAMR National Enterprise Registration Information System.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum registered capital applies to an ordinary wholly foreign-owned limited liability company under current Chinese law. The registered capital amount and contribution schedule must be stated in the Articles of Association and the capital must be genuinely subscribed and paid within the agreed period. No blocked escrow account is required by law at the time of incorporation; however, foreign-invested capital paid in from outside China must complete SAFE foreign exchange registration and be settled through a domestic foreign exchange capital account.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION NO. 2025-001 OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF CN_WFOE_LTD

The first meeting of the board of directors of CN_WFOE_LTD (the Company) was duly convened and held on ________ at ________ at the registered office of the Company and by remote video conference. The following directors were present in person or by proxy: [Director A], [Director B], and [Director C], constituting a quorum under the Articles of Association of the Company and the Company Law of the People's Republic of China. The chairman of the meeting confirmed that proper notice had been given and that the agenda was lawful.

After deliberation, the board unanimously adopted the following resolutions:

1. Subscription and Share Capital. The board approved the registered capital of the Company as ________, divided into ________ shares, to be subscribed by the sole member in accordance with the capital contribution schedule set out in the Articles of Association. The board authorized the legal representative to issue capital contribution calls, to open any collection account required for paid-in capital, and to issue capital contribution certificates after verified payment.

2. Banking. The board approved the opening of a basic deposit account, a capital settlement account, and a foreign exchange capital account with [Bank]. The board appointed [Chairman], [Chief Financial Officer], and [Treasurer] as account signatories, with all payments above an approved threshold requiring dual signatures, and instructed the bank signatories to execute the relevant account-opening forms and operating agreements.

3. Registered Office. The board confirmed that the registered office of the Company shall be at ________, that such address is lawfully occupied by the Company under a valid lease or ownership instrument, and that the Company shall file a registration amendment if the registered office changes.

4. Statutory Officers. The board appointed [Name] as Chairman and legal representative, [Name] as General Manager, [Name] as Chief Financial Officer, [Name] as Head of Operations, and [Name] as Supervisor, each for a term of three years, with powers and duties as specified in the Company Law and the Articles of Association.

5. Licensing and Compliance. The board instructed management to apply without delay for all necessary special equipment manufacturing licenses, environmental impact assessment approvals, fire safety certificates, civil defense clearances, and workplace safety permits required for the manufacture of overhead and gantry cranes.

6. Seals and Ancillary Approvals. The board approved the creation of the company chop, financial chop, invoice chop, contract chop, and legal representative chop at a public security-approved engraving unit, and authorized the registration of such chops in accordance with applicable rules.

7. Delegation. The board authorized the Chairman and any one director jointly to execute all documents, complete all filings with the market regulation authority, tax authority, bank, and State Administration of Foreign Exchange, and perform all incidental acts necessary to give effect to these resolutions.

All resolutions were passed unanimously and are effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Pre-Approval and Foreign Investor Document Authentication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Registration Information Portal, with apostille or consular authentication authorities for the investor's home jurisdiction
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit to the National Enterprise Registration Information System a name pre-approval application for the wholly foreign-owned enterprise, providing the Chinese and English company name, intended business scope covering the manufacture of cranes and hoisting gear, proposed registered address, and investor identity. The system will screen against existing registered names, prohibited terms, and public interest restrictions. In parallel, the foreign investor’s incorporation certificate, certificate of good standing, board resolution authorizing establishment, and passport or power-of-attorney of the appointed legal representative must be notarized in the home jurisdiction and issued with an Apostille certificate or, for non-Hague jurisdictions, legalized by a People's Republic of China embassy or consulate, then translated into Chinese by a qualified translation company. All translated documents must carry the translator's seal and the original documents must be preserved for submission with copies.
required_dossiers: Name pre-approval application form
Investor's certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing
Apostilled or legalized board resolution authorizing formation
Power of attorney appointing the authorized signatory
Passport copies of directors, supervisor, and legal representative
Certified Chinese translations of all foreign-language documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, the system provides a rejection reason code; the applicant may select an alternate name and resubmit immediately. If the apostille or authentication certificate is challenged, contact the issuing competent authority for a corrected certificate and resubmit without penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Approval of Articles of Association and Governance Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Foreign investor, founding board of directors, and local SAMR acceptance desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Association in Chinese and English, ensuring that the Chinese version is controlling. The Articles must specify registered capital, share classes, capital contribution method and time, composition of the board of directors, legal representative, supervisor, profit distribution, liquidation, and rights of the foreign investor. The founding members must then hold a formal organizational meeting to adopt the Articles and issue the first board resolution, which is a mandatory registration prerequisite. For a manufacturing entity producing overhead and gantry cranes, the Articles should also authorize special equipment licensing procedures, environmental compliance undertakings, and post-registration bank and foreign exchange filings. Once signed, the Articles and related governance consents are prepared for submission to SAMR.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association in Chinese and English
Founding shareholder resolution adopting the Articles
First board resolution approving governance and officers
Lease agreement or title certificate for the proposed registered office
Consent letters from all directors, supervisor, and managers
Legal representative appointment form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SAMR queries any Article as inconsistent with mandatory Company Law provisions, adopt a supplemental shareholder or board resolution to amend the clause and resubmit. If the notarial certificate contains a defect, obtain a corrected certificate from the same notary or authentication office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Establishment Registration and Issuance of Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipal or provincial Market Supervision Administration, through the SAMR one-stop online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the enterprise establishment registration through the SAMR online system, attaching the approved name certificate, authenticated investor documents, signed Articles of Association, identity documents of all officers, address proof for the proposed registered office, and the lawful use declaration for the production site. The system generates a Unified Social Credit Code and, after legal review, the registration authority issues the Business License. The business scope must be drafted with precision to include 'manufacture of overhead and gantry cranes, hoisting machinery, and special handling equipment; installation, maintenance, transformation and repair of special equipment' so that subsequent industrial licensing proceeds without a re-registration. After issuance, verify that the registered information exactly matches the approved scope and Articles, and immediately correct any typographical or clerical error through a change registration.
required_dossiers: Establishment registration application form
Name pre-approval certificate
Apostilled or legalized investor documents and Chinese translations
Signed Articles of Association
Identity and qualification documents of legal representative, directors, supervisors, and managers
Registered office lease, title certificate, and landlord consent
Power of attorney for the filing agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended, provide the requested corrective documentation through the SAMR portal and resubmit. If the Business License is issued with an inaccurate scope or officer name, apply for a formal alteration registration immediately and before applying for any industrial license.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Corporate Formalities: Seals, Bank Accounts, Tax and Foreign Exchange Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public security-licensed seal engraving units; People's Bank of China-supervised commercial banks; State Taxation Administration (STA); State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the Business License, engage a public security-licensed seal engraving unit to produce the company chop, financial chop, invoice chop, contract chop, and legal representative chop. Open a basic deposit account at a bank selected by the board and obtain the deposit account registration certificate. Complete tax registration through the STA electronic tax portal within 30 days, including value-added tax general taxpayer status, corporate income tax, stamp duty, payroll withholding registration, and invoice quota application. Simultaneously apply to SAFE for the WFOE foreign exchange registration and open a foreign exchange capital account to receive and settle the foreign investor's paid-in capital. Register the employer with local social insurance, medical insurance, unemployment insurance, work injury insurance, maternity insurance, and housing fund authorities.
required_dossiers: Original Business License
Company chop, financial chop, and legal representative chop
Board resolution approving bank account opening and signatories
Tax registration application form and business license
SAFE foreign exchange registration form and capital account application
Articles of Association and lease agreement
Director, supervisor, and legal representative identity documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank or SAFE requires supplementary materials, furnish the relevant board resolution, Articles of Association, or capital contribution schedule. If tax registration is delayed due to system outage, obtain a system confirmation notice and apply for waiver of any late-filing penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Special Equipment Manufacturing License Application and Product Type Testing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) Special Equipment Safety Supervision Bureau; provincial market supervision department; authorized special equipment inspection agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before commencing crane production, submit a formal application for the Special Equipment Production License for hoisting machinery, specifically covering overhead and gantry crane manufacturing. The applicant must demonstrate a quality assurance system in accordance with the Special Equipment Production License rules, including design control, material inspection, welding procedures, non-destructive testing, machining, assembly, painting, final inspection, and after-sales service. The product models intended for manufacture must pass type testing by an authorized special equipment testing authority, and the plant must be able to demonstrate load testing of prototype cranes to applicable GB/T standards. After a document review and on-site factory inspection, the licensing authority will issue a license specifying approved product categories and parameters. Production cannot lawfully begin before the license is granted.
required_dossiers: Special equipment manufacturing license application form
Business License and legal representative identity certificate
Quality assurance manual and process control procedures
Design drawings and calculation reports for each crane model
Type test report and prototype load test certificate
List of production machinery, welding equipment, and testing instruments
Welder and non-destructive testing personnel certificates
Factory layout drawing, EIA approval, and fire safety acceptance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the licensing authority issues a defect correction notice, implement corrective actions in the quality system, document the changes, and submit a revised application for re-inspection. If the product type test is unsuccessful, modify the design, recalculate, and retest at the authorized inspection institution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental Impact Assessment, Civil Defense Fire Permit, and Occupational Safety Pre-Start Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal Ecology and Environment Bureau; Municipal Fire and Rescue Department; Municipal Bureau of Emergency Management; local health authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before construction or production commences, file the project with the municipal ecology and environment bureau. A crane manufacturing plant with metal fabrication, welding, painting, and assembly operations will ordinarily require an Environmental Impact Report Form, or a Full Environmental Impact Report if located in an ecologically sensitive area. Obtain an environmental approval document, construct pollution control facilities, and complete environmental protection acceptance before trial production. Obtain fire protection design review and fire safety acceptance certification for factory workshops, storage areas, paint rooms, and electrical rooms. For large-span crane manufacturing bays and crane runway structures, arrange structural load inspection by a qualified civil engineer and, where required, a Civil Defense fire permit. File an occupational hazard risk evaluation with the local health authority and register hazardous chemical storage areas for paints and solvents.
required_dossiers: Environmental impact assessment application and technical report
EIA approval document or registration receipt
Fire protection design drawings and fire safety acceptance application
Structural calculations and load test reports for crane runways
Occupational health pre-evaluation report
Hazardous chemical storage inventory and material safety data sheets
Emergency response plan and tabletop drill records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ecology and environment bureau rejects the EIA, revise the report according to the expert review opinions and resubmit. If the fire department identifies fire safety deficiencies, install the required suppression and protection systems and request re-inspection. The plant must not begin operations until all certificates are issued.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) Special Equipment Safety Supervision Bureau, provincial market supervision departments, and the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology for industrial policy and equipment manufacturing guidance
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Special Equipment Production License for Hoisting Machinery (overhead and gantry crane manufacturing category), issued under the Special Equipment Safety Law and the SAMR Special Equipment Production License Rules

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE) and the project-site municipal or provincial ecology and environment bureau
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Environmental Impact Report Form (Category II) for a standard crane manufacturing and assembly facility; upgraded to a Full Environmental Impact Report (Category I) if the project is located in an ecologically sensitive or protected area; ancillary auxiliary projects may qualify for Environmental Registration (Category III) only where no significant pollution is generated
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater treatment effluent must comply with applicable Chinese discharge standards, including pH 6-9, COD not exceeding 100 mg/L, NH3-N not exceeding 15 mg/L, suspended solids not exceeding 70 mg/L, and petroleum oil not exceeding 5 mg/L. Paint booth and coating exhaust must be treated so that filterable particulate matter does not exceed 30 mg/m3 and non-methane total hydrocarbons (NMHC) in stack exhaust do not exceed 60 mg/m3, with factory boundary fugitive NMHC not exceeding 2.0 mg/m3. Hazardous wastes, including paint residue, waste solvents, wastewater treatment sludge, and oil-contaminated rags, must be stored in sealed and labeled containers at a permitted hazardous waste storage point, transferred under manifest control to a licensed hazardous waste treatment contractor, and may not be stored for more than one year.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire protection design review and fire safety acceptance certificate or filing receipt from the municipal Fire and Rescue Department for the manufacturing workshop, warehouses, painting area, electrical rooms, and hazardous material storage. Civil Defense clearance and structural load inspection for large-span crane manufacturing bays and crane runway beams must be certified by a registered structural engineer. Special equipment use registration must be obtained for each crane and pressure equipment before operation. Occupational health clearance must confirm that workers exposed to noise, welding fumes, and paint vapors receive pre-employment and periodic medical examinations, and that the workplace meets the requirements of the Law on Prevention and Control of Occupational Diseases and relevant workplace safety regulations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China; online electronic portal: Electronic Tax Administration (E-Tax) of the State Taxation Administration, accessible through the national unified tax service platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident shareholder establishing a wholly foreign-owned enterprise, the shareholder does not automatically receive a Chinese Tax Identification Number; the WFOE itself must complete tax registration. Step 1: obtain the business license from the local Administration for Market Regulation. Step 2: complete taxpayer registration with the State Taxation Administration through the E-Tax platform within 30 days of business license issuance. Step 3: submit the articles of association, incorporation certificate, legal representative identification, registered address proof, shareholder information, and capital verification documents as required. Step 4: the State Taxation Administration assigns the statutory Taxpayer Identification Number embedded in the Unified Social Credit Code and activates tax filing, invoice management, and taxpayer status. Step 5: complete VAT taxpayer status determination, banking account filing, and E-Invoice activation. A non-resident parent with China-sourced income is generally subject to withholding at source without separate TIN registration unless it establishes a permanent establishment in China.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise Limited Liability Company is a Chinese resident enterprise taxed directly on worldwide income, with no pass-through transparency.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for entity classification under the Enterprise Income Tax; available VAT status election between General VAT Taxpayer and Small-Scale VAT Taxpayer based on annual taxable sales threshold, subject to State Taxation Administration approval.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: All incorporated enterprises must register for tax upon establishment; annual taxable sales above RMB 5,000,000 triggers mandatory General VAT Taxpayer registration, while below that threshold the enterprise may register as a Small-Scale VAT Taxpayer.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The enterprise must issue Special VAT Invoices or Fully Digitalized Electronic Invoices through the State Taxation Administration's E-Invoice Platform; invoices are generated with a unique digital stamp and reported in real time to tax authorities through application programming interfaces or the tax control device, with no need for physical stamps on fully digitalized electronic invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Direct export of manufactured port container gantry cranes and hoisting gear qualifies for the 0% VAT export rate and corresponding export tax rebate when the goods physically leave the customs territory of China, are declared under customs supervision through China International Trade Single Window, and the export proceeds are repatriated and verified with the customs and foreign exchange administrations.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration generated through China International Trade Single Window
Bill of Lading or multimodal transport document
Bank receipt or foreign exchange settlement certificate evidencing repatriation of export proceeds
Special VAT Invoice or ordinary export invoice for the exported goods
Export sales contract and commercial invoice
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Tax authorities may conduct export tax rebate audits using customs electronic declaration data, logistics records, and foreign exchange verification information; any false export declaration, fake invoices, or non-repatriation of proceeds triggers recovery of the zero-rated refund, late payment surcharge, and a penalty of 50% up to five times the amount of tax involved under the Tax Administration Law and its implementing regulations, in addition to criminal liability for fraudulent export tax refunds under the Criminal Law.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) under the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China operates a bifurcated foreign exchange regulatory framework. The current account, which covers trade in goods, services, and routine profit remittances, is largely convertible, subject to genuine transaction verification and documentary compliance under the Foreign Exchange Administration Regulations and the SAFE counterparty verification system. By contrast, the capital account remains heavily controlled, requiring case-by-case approval, registration, or filing with SAFE and its local branches. A Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) must register its foreign direct investment (FDI) equity injection under the Foreign Investment Information Report and obtain a Foreign Exchange Registration Certificate for FDI, after which the injected capital is credited to a Capital Account (FDI Capability Account). Surrender requirements apply to export receipts: under the 2019 SAFE circular on optimizing trade foreign exchange administration, export proceeds in goods may be retained offshore or repatriated but must be repatriated to China within the statutory time limit if the exporter opts for onshore settlement, and banks supervise the authenticity and consistency of trade background documents. Profit remittance hurdles include the requirement of prior year audited financial statements, tax clearance certificates, board resolution on dividend distribution, and proof that registered capital has been fully injected if required by the articles of association. A WFOE may distribute profits only from after-tax earnings under Chinese GAAP, and the remittance of dividends is treated as a current account transaction once the capital verification and SAFE filing are complete, although banks still apply a strict know-your-customer review on the ultimate beneficial owner and the underlying business rationale. The overall assessment is that the Chinese yuan is not freely convertible on the capital account; current account convertibility is real but administratively intensive, and any cross-border capital movement requires a clear regulatory paper trail through SAFE-approved banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For general trade exports, repatriation of goods trade foreign exchange receipts is required within 180 days from the date of export declaration unless a prior SAFE extension or offshore retention registration is obtained; after repatriation, the exporter may keep the proceeds in a foreign currency settlement account with a domestic bank or convert into CNY voluntarily, and there is no mandatory conversion ratio for most ordinary manufacturing exporters under the current SAFE administration, except where the bank flags false trade or the exporter is on a special monitoring list requiring full surrender and transaction-level verification.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech electronic money institutions and digital banking platforms are generally not viable as primary treasury conduits for a China mainland WFOE. Chinese foreign exchange regulations require that cross-border receipts and payments be routed through banks that have obtained the relevant foreign exchange settlement and sale license from SAFE, and that the counterparty bank be a licensed financial institution in the jurisdiction of the transaction. Pure-play offshore EMIs that do not maintain a physical branch or licensed presence in China and that are not qualified foreign exchange designated banks cannot execute SAFE reporting, capital account registration verification, or export proceeds surrender reconciliation on behalf of a WFOE. Their utility is limited to auxiliary functions such as pre-onboarding account aggregation, payment tracking dashboards, or treasury visibility, but they must not displace domestic bank settlement rails. Legal constraints under the Administrative Measures for the Payment Services of Non-Financial Institutions and PBOC regulations on payment providers further prohibit unlicensed entities from engaging in currency conversion and cross-border settlement services for resident onshore entities. The feasible approach is to use a licensed domestic tier-1 bank as the settlement anchor and, if required, integrate an offshore EMI only as a non-account information aggregator for group-level cash visibility outside China.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a WFOE opening a corporate bank account in China, the statutory legal representative and the designated authorized signatories are generally required to appear physically before the bank's compliance officers in-branch for identity verification and the obligatory KYC interview. In practice, major domestic banks also accept remote consular notarization and apostilled power-of-attorney packages for the non-resident ultimate beneficial owners, but at least one onshore senior officer, typically the legal representative or the general manager whose identity is filed with the State Administration for Market Regulation, must be present onshore for biometric verification and to sign the account opening documents. Remote opening through consular proxy is not a recognized standard for first-time corporate account establishment in China; banks require the physical presence of the statutory representative or a locally registered authorized person who can present the original business license, company chop, and personal identification. In exceptional cross-border holding situations, a branch-approved special arrangement can be made where the legal representative appears before a Chinese embassy or consulate to complete a notarized affidavit and the bank accepts it after a senior compliance committee review, but this is discretionary and subject to higher due diligence thresholds including video interviews and confirmation of the corporate seal policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner sits in a jurisdiction with high money-laundering risk or involves multiple layered holding companies, triggering enhanced due diligence under PBOC Beneficial Owner Identification Measures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete corporate ownership cascade from each shareholder to the natural-person UBO, certified copies of passports, board resolutions appointing directors, a group structure chart stamped by the overseas parent, a written explanation of the source of wealth and source of funds for the injected capital, bank reference letters from the ultimate parent's nominated bank in its home jurisdiction, and a sworn affidavit confirming no politically exposed person status where relevant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business scope covers port machinery manufacturing that may involve export-controlled or dual-use equipment, triggering trade-based money laundering scrutiny and end-user due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed product catalog and technical specifications demonstrating commercial nature, absence of military or dual-use classifications, the ISIC 2816 trade license or business scope certificate, export trade contracts with bona fide overseas port operators or general contractors, end-user certificates from disclosed final customers, compliance manuals for export control screening against UN sanctions lists, and annual external audit reports confirming revenue recognition consistency.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border capital injection structure involves parent financing through shareholder loans combined with equity contributions, creating ambiguity around the true source of funds and potential round-tripping.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A notarized and apostilled board resolution from the sole shareholder or joint venture board approving the exact capital injection mix, signed shareholder loan agreements with commercial-rate interest terms, bank statements from the remitting parent account showing the funds originated from operating revenue or a disclosed external financing facility, the SAFE Foreign Investment Information Report confirmation, a capital verification report from a licensed Chinese CPA firm after funds land in the FDI capital account, and an undertaking that shareholder loans will be converted or repaid under SAFE debt-to-equity rules.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The bank's internal sanction screening flags the offshore parent or its directors on politically exposed person or sanctions advisory lists due to name similarity or previous corporate domicile in a sanctioned-adjacent jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full legal opinion from an internationally recognized law firm on the entity's ownership and control chain, comprehensive sanctions screening reports from reputable screening providers covering the entity, all shareholders, directors, and UBOs with resolution of any fuzzy-hit alarms, a joint affidavit from shareholders explaining the rationale for any previous offshore domicile, audited financial statements for the past three years, and a compliance presentation pack with false-positive analysis evidence for the bank's sanctions committee.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For an inbound capital injection into a WFOE, the routing protocol begins with the sponsor filing the Foreign Investment Information Report with the local Administration for Market Regulation or through the Ministry of Commerce reporting system, followed by opening a Capital Account (FDI Capability Account) at a SAFE-designated domestic bank in the WFOE's name. The overseas parent then wires the equity funds via SWIFT MT103 with the transaction purpose code designated for foreign direct investment, typically codes under the International Transaction Reporting System such as 'FDI equity contribution' or 'foreign exchange registration for direct investment', and the remittance instruction must include the SAFE registration number and the WFOE's name exactly as registered. The receiving bank will verify the capital account registration information against the SAFE system, confirm the transaction can only be credited to the Capital Account and not to a current account, and process the funds as pending for the purpose of a post-arrival capital verification by a licensed CPA firm. The CPA issues a capital verification report confirming the contribution is fully paid after the funds are received and the bank provides a Foreign Exchange Receipt Confirmation. The proceeds in the Capital Account can be used only for actual business purposes in compliance with the negative list, after which they may be transferred to the operational current account for permissible working capital expenditure if supported by invoices, contracts, and tax invoices from third parties. Any subsequent increase or decrease in registered capital requires an updated Foreign Investment Information Report and SAFE filing.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for the manufacture and sale of port container gantry cranes should be settled primarily through commercial letters of credit, documentary collections, and SWIFT MT103 wire transfers, all subject to the bank's trade authenticity review and SAFE's overall trade monitoring framework. For import of key components, a WFOE can open an irrevocable usance LC at its domestic bank with a SWIFT MT700 issuance, with the documentary package comprising a commercial invoice, bill of lading, insurance policy, packing list, and a certificate of quality; the bank will release payment against compliant presentation under UCP 600. For export sales to overseas port operators, the WFOE as beneficiary should receive LCs from the buyer's overseas bank, or if the buyer pays by documentary collections, the WFOE's bank acts as presenting bank under the Incoterms agreed in the contract, typically CIF or CIP for heavy machinery with marine cargo insurance. Where direct wire payment is used for spare parts or pre-shipment advances, the remittance purpose code for export trade should be selected so that the receipts can be matched with the customs export declaration in the SAFE monitoring system, thereby satisfying the 'goods, funds, and declaration consistency' principle. Disbursement of project escrow funds, as required by the entity's target payment rails, should be executed through a domestic bank's project clearing desk, using an escrow agreement and milestone-based inspection certificates to release funds under an onshore trust or escrow account, ensuring each disbursement is backed by valid VAT special invoices and customs clearance records.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore RMB forward contracts (FX forwards) with a licensed domestic bank, available only for genuine hedging of documented trade exposures and current-account transactions, requiring underlying contracts and business licences for each transaction.

Over-the-counter currency swaps between CNY and major convertible currencies for approved current-account and capital-project cash-flow matching, executed through SAFE-registered domestic banks with real demand and risk exposure verification.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in offshore CNH markets may be considered only for group-level management of RMB volatility outside China, but cannot be settled onshore and do not replace the legally recognized onshore CNY hedging market; onshore hedging must be executed via the China Foreign Exchange Trade System with SAFE approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Settlement Filing and Payment (CIT reconciliation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent State Taxation Administration (STA) tax service bureau controlling the WFOE registration; filed through the integrated electronic tax portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 May of the following year for the immediately preceding calendar year; no automatic extension in normal circumstances
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is subject to an administrative fine of up to RMB 10,000 (RMB 20,000 in serious cases) and a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax for each overdue day; understatement or fraudulent miscalculation can attract a penalty of 50% to 5 times the underpaid tax plus criminal referral for tax evasion; continued non-compliance may be transmitted to the market regulator and can lead to SAMR business license revocation and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Enterprise Annual Report on Information Publicity (annual market regulation filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and local market regulation bureau via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 January to 30 June for the prior calendar year; the WFOE must report within the statutory window irrespective of anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file by 30 June results in inclusion in the List of Enterprises Operating Abnormally within 10 working days; after three consecutive years of non-rectification, the WFOE is placed on the List of Seriously Illegal and Untrustworthy Enterprises; the company, directors, and legal representative are then subject to cross-department restrictions on taxation, banking, procurement, entry-exit, and credit status, and SAMR may ultimately revoke the business license and trigger administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Information Annual Report for Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) and SAMR through the integrated foreign investment information report system; information shared with tax, foreign exchange, and statistics authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 30 June for the preceding calendar year, aligned with the SAMR Enterprise Annual Report window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or filing false information is punishable by an order to rectify, recording of non-compliance in the enterprise credit file, and administrative fines under the Foreign Investment Law and Company Registration Regulations; sustained failure to report can be combined with the SAMR Serious Illegal and Untrustworthy Enterprise list and support revocation of the business licence and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Audit of Financial Statements and Shareholder Adoption of Audited Accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Audited financial statements must be prepared for the shareholders meeting of the WFOE and retained on file for inspection by SAMR, STA, and SAFE; no government filing fee is payable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within six months after the fiscal year end (by 30 June following the year end); the audited report must be finalized before the 31 May CIT filing where the tax return relies on audited figures
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to audit violates PRC Company Law and renders profit distribution and reserve allocation unlawful; responsible directors and officers may be liable to administrative fines and compensation; in tax verification proceedings the absence of an audit report is treated as an adverse factor and can attract the 50%-5x underpaid tax penalty plus credit-file association with SAMR, with ultimate risk of licence revocation and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Direct Investment Operating Information Declaration (FDI and SAFE data confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through the integrated SAMR/MOFCOM annual report system and the bank handling the WFOE's foreign exchange registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 30 June for the prior year; any change in shareholding, registered capital, or foreign investor control must additionally be reported within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-reporting or false reporting may cause suspension of foreign exchange settlement, capital account transactions, dividend remittances, and equity transfer foreign exchange proceeds until rectification; SAFE may impose warnings and fines up to RMB 300,000 under the Foreign Exchange Administrative Regulations; persistent non-compliance is referenced in the enterprise credit record and can contribute to administrative strike-off action by SAMR.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Pollutant Discharge Permit Execution Report (where the crane manufacturing site holds a discharge permit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Municipal Ecology and Environment Bureau responsible for the production site's pollutant discharge permit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 January for the prior reporting year; monthly and quarterly execution reports are also required depending on the specific permit conditions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under the Environmental Protection Law and Pollution Prevention and Control Laws, failure to submit or false submission of the execution report may attract fines up to RMB 500,000, daily continuous penalties for ongoing violations, permit suspension or revocation, and joint credit discipline that can be escalated to SAMR for license strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: PRC Company Law imposes an unconditional statutory audit on every limited liability company, including a WFOE, at the end of each fiscal year; there is no exemption based on balance-sheet size, turnover, or headcount. The entity-based trigger is registration as a company under PRC Company Law, not a quantitative metric. For classification and administrative reporting purposes, an industrial enterprise with annual main operating revenue exceeding RMB 20 million (approximately USD 2.8 million) is an above-designated-size enterprise and is expected to maintain auditor-supported financial declarations; an enterprise with total assets above RMB 100 million, turnover above RMB 100 million, or more than 200 employees may be classified as a medium- or large-size enterprise, but classification does not create or waive the audit obligation. The legal audit trigger also extends to any WFOE applying for dividend distribution, foreign exchange repatriation, equity transfer approval, bank credit facilities, tax refunds, government subsidies, or liquidation, because all such procedures require audited or CPA-certified financial information.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (CAS / China GAAP), substantially converged with IFRS, are the mandatory framework for the statutory accounts and for the Chinese CPA audit report; the Enterprise Accounting Standard for Small Enterprises may be used only by qualifying small-scale Chinese entities that do not need a full CAS presentation, but a WFOE under audit should present full CAS statements where the audit opinion is required for tax, foreign exchange, or creditor purposes; statements must be denominated in RMB with Chinese language presentation, and English translations may be prepared for the foreign parent.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the PBOC and SAMR Beneficial-Owner Information Management Measures, a WFOE must file initial beneficial owner particulars identifying natural persons who ultimately own at least 25% of equity or voting rights, or who otherwise exercise actual control; any change in shareholding, voting control, senior management control, or beneficial ownership must be reported to SAMR within 30 calendar days of the change; each year, the WFOE must re-confirm and warrant the accuracy of the last-filed UBO information within the SAMR Enterprise Annual Report due by 30 June; a change in registered shareholders is effective against third parties only after SAMR change registration, and the application must be submitted within 30 days of the internal equity-transfer resolution and execution of the transfer agreement.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 to USD 2,000 per year for a compliant registered address, corporate secretarial record maintenance, and annual report preparation support in major commercial cities; industrial production site lease and local compliance services are additional
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 to USD 12,000 for a Chinese local CPA firm audit of a manufacturing WFOE with inventory and foreign-exchange activity; USD 15,000 to USD 30,000 for Big Four or international network audit where the US or EU parent requires IFRS or US-equivalent reporting packs and complex intercompany transactions

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The 25% statutory state rate may be reduced to 15% for High and New Technology Enterprises; qualifying port crane manufacturers can also use accelerated depreciation and an R&D super-deduction, currently up to 100% additional deduction of qualifying R&D expenses. There is no blanket free-zone rate for ordinary mainland WFOEs, but certain encouraged industries in Western China can access a 15% rate until the end of the preferential window.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: People's Republic of China Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return (Form A, A-class taxpayer) filed through the State Taxation Administration electronic tax filing portal; quarterly prepayment returns are made on the same A-class simplified schedule.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly advance filings plus one annual final reconciliation; annual return is filed after the fiscal year-end.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly prepayment must be filed within 15 calendar days after the end of each calendar quarter; the annual final Corporate Income Tax return must be filed on or before 31 May of the year following the tax year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total operating revenue, comprising sales of port container gantry cranes, spare parts, reconditioning services, and after-sales maintenance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all revenue recognized under PRC Accounting Standards for the WFOE as a resident enterprise. Exclude VAT separately. For sales to a non-resident parent or affiliated distributor, book the arm's length price supported by a transfer pricing analysis; any artificial under-invoicing of export revenue must be reversed before filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating costs, including steel, electrical systems, gearboxes, imported components, direct labor, and manufacturing overhead of the crane production line.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Support import costs with customs declarations, invoices, and contracts. Related-party purchase prices must be tested under the Comparable Uncontrolled Price or Cost Plus method. Do not include customs VAT or surcharges that are recoverable as input VAT; non-resident parent allocation of manufacturing costs must be documented under an actual cost-contribution arrangement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling expenses, including transport of cranes to ports, project commissioning agents, warranty costs, and export trade commissions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Entertainment expenses are deductible only within statutory ratio caps. Commission paid to a foreign affiliate must pass the arm's length standard and must be reviewed for Chinese-sourced service income; if the commission creates a service performed in China, withholding tax and Business Tax obligations may arise.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Administrative expenses, including management staff, legal, accounting, office overhead, and research-and-development administrative support.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disallow related-party management fees paid directly to the foreign parent because such fees are non-deductible under Chinese tax law. Head-office service charges can be recognized only if supported by actual service contracts, invoice records, and proof that no duplicative costs are deducted by the foreign parent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial expenses, comprising interest on bank loans, intercompany financing, bank charges, and foreign-exchange losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest on intercompany debt is deductible only within the 2:1 debt-to-equity thin-capitalization safe harbor for a non-financial WFOE; excessive interest is disallowed and may be recharacterized as a dividend. Interest remitted to a foreign related lender is subject to non-resident withholding tax of 10% unless a lower treaty rate is substantiated by a Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership declaration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating income, including gains on disposal of fixed assets, government subsidies, insurance proceeds, and penalty recoveries.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tax government subsidies unless they are within a recognized tax-exempt catalogue. Gains on a disposal of shares in the WFOE by the non-resident shareholder are generally not taxed in the WFOE return; however, any profit generated through the WFOE's assets must be fully disclosed to avoid classification as hidden taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating expenses, including charitable donations, asset write-offs, and losses on disposed production lines.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Charitable donations are deductible up to 12% of annual accounting profit, with a carryforward for excess qualifying donations; fines, tax penalties, criminal fines, and illegal expenditure are not deductible. Losses must be evidenced by board resolutions and asset-disposal vouchers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting total profit before tax computed under China Accounting Standards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the bridge between the US GAAP or IFRS pack and PRC taxable income. The WFOE must reconcile foreign parent group-reporting profit to the Chinese return; top-up adjustments cannot be made for non-resident withholding tax or treaty-covered income not connected with the WFOE's operation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustment increase or decrease, covering non-deductible items, fair-value differences, particularity adjustments, and transfer pricing rectification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter all Schedule A-type adjustment lines, including transfer pricing corrections, thin-capitalization add-backs, and R&D super-deduction decreases. Cross-border documentation must be available before claiming a reduction; absent contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation, the tax authority may rely on its statutory comparables and impose the higher taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after all statutory adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE's taxable income is taxed at entity level; profits attributable to the non-resident parent only become subject to a separate dividends withholding tax once actually distributed. Do not confuse taxable income in Box 10 with distributable profit subject to non-resident withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable Corporate Income Tax rate and concessional rate used for reporting.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE holds High and New Technology Enterprise status, claim the 15% rate and file the relevant supporting schedule. A treaty reduction applies to a non-resident shareholder's dividend withholding, not to the WFOE's own corporate income tax rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, prepayments already made, and final balance of tax due or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim foreign tax credits only for underlying foreign income taxes paid by the WFOE's branches abroad. Quarterly prepayments must be reconciled; any withholding tax withheld from a non-resident recipient is not a credit against the WFOE's Corporate Income Tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the quarterly or annual Corporate Income Tax return attracts an administrative late-filing penalty of RMB 2,000, increasing to RMB 2,000-10,000 in serious cases. Unpaid tax accrues a daily overdue surcharge of 0.05%. False or fraudulent under-declaration triggers the Tax Collection Law tax-evasion penalty of 50% to 500% of the evaded tax, plus possible criminal prosecution under Article 201 of the PRC Criminal Law, with imprisonment for up to seven years and fines where the evaded amount is substantial.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory withholding tax on dividends distributed by a resident WFOE to a non-resident enterprise, reduced to a lower treaty ceiling only where the non-resident recipient is the beneficial owner and all procedural requirements are satisfied.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before making an outbound dividend payment, the WFOE as withholding agent must file a non-resident withholding declaration with the State Taxation Administration and collect from the non-resident shareholder a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority, a beneficial ownership statement, and documentary evidence of the shareholding chain. The tax bureau may request proof that the recipient has economic substance, that the dividend is not routed through a conduit entity, and that the beneficial-owner test under the applicable Double Tax Treaty is met. If treaty relief is not approved before remittance, the statutory 10% must be withheld and the non-resident can apply for a refund through the administrative treaty-relief procedure within the statutory claim period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for the use of industrial patents or manufacturing know-how carry a 10% statutory withholding tax; most DTA treaties reduce royalties to 5%-10%, but only where a royalty is genuinely paid for technical services and not recharacterized as a dividend. Interest paid to non-resident lenders is taxed at the statutory 10% rate, with treaty relief generally between 7% and 10% in widely used DTA conventions; interest paid to a shareholder with no economic substance can be fully denied treaty relief and reclassified as a dividend.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File documentation must be prepared when the WFOE's intercompany transactions exceed RMB 200 million for tangible goods, RMB 100 million for intangible property or financial transactions, and RMB 40 million for other intercompany transactions in a single fiscal year. A Master File must be prepared where aggregate related-party transactions exceed RMB 1 billion or the multinational group meets the Country-by-Country reporting revenue threshold of approximately RMB 5.5 billion consolidated group revenue.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Mainland China does not operate a standard OECD Economic Substance Regulations registry, but tax authorities apply the General Anti-Avoidance Rule, substance-over-form, and beneficial-ownership doctrines. For a port crane WFOE, the Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) are procurement of steel and components, crane design adaptation, component assembly, quality assurance, shipping, and after-sales project support; those functions and risks must be performed and managed by substantive employees in mainland China. If intangible development, enhancement, maintenance, protection, and exploitation are artificially split from the WFOE without actual decision-making in the Chinese entity, profits can be reallocated and treaty benefits denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE sells overhead cargo cranes and gantry crane spare parts to an affiliated offshore distributor at artificially low prices, retaining profits in a zero-tax jurisdiction while the Chinese entity loses money; contemporaneous transfer pricing files are fabricated and quarterly returns understate taxable revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 41, the tax authority makes a transfer pricing adjustment and recomputes taxable income. Tax Collection Law Article 63 imposes a daily 0.05% overdue surcharge and a penalty of 50% to 500% of the under-paid tax; the adjustment is not limited by the rate reduction and can be assessed retroactively where fraud is proven.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The courts may pierce the WFOE's limited liability shield if directors personally signed false invoices, fake service contracts, or misleading transfer pricing documentation. Directors become jointly and severally liable for the recovered tax and penalties, their personal assets may be frozen, they are subject to cross-border exit bans under the dishonest-judgment-debtor blacklisting system, and they can be prosecuted for tax evasion under Article 201 of the Criminal Law, leading to imprisonment for up to seven years where the evaded amount is large.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A non-resident intermediate shareholder incorporated in a tax-treaty jurisdiction has no employees, no physical office, no board meetings, and no independent decision-making; the WFOE channels dividend and royalty payments through that conduit solely to claim a reduced Double Tax Treaty withholding rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority invokes the beneficial-ownership rule and the General Anti-Avoidance Rule under Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 47 to deny the treaty claim, reclassifies the payment as a taxable dividend, recovers the 10% statutory withholding tax, and adds surcharges and fines of 50% to 500% of the under-withheld amount under the Tax Collection Law. The conduit entity may also be deemed to have a permanent establishment in China.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the WFOE and of the intermediary who knowingly sign false beneficial-ownership declarations or misrepresent the foreign entity's substance face personal civil restitution for the unpaid withholding tax, attachment of personal assets, travel bans, and criminal liability for fraudulent tax avoidance. If the sham scheme is used to evade taxes, the statutory criminal punishment can include imprisonment and forfeiture of proceeds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Agent Failure and Non-Filing of Dividend Remittance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE declares a dividend, wire-transfers profits to the non-resident parent, and deliberately fails to withhold the 10% non-resident Corporate Income Tax on dividends; it also misses the quarterly and annual Corporate Income Tax filing deadlines and operates entirely outside the electronic tax filing system.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority orders the WFOE to remit the unwithheld tax, with a daily late-interest rate of 0.05%; under Tax Collection Law Article 62, late filing penalties of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 apply, and, where the failure to withhold is deliberate, a penalty of 50% to 300% of the tax that was not withheld. If the non-filing is part of an intentional tax-evasion plan, Article 63 penalties of 50% to 500% of evaded tax and criminal prosecution apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorized the dividend distribution without a tax withholding certificate can be held personally liable for the missing tax because their act contravenes the mandatory withholding obligation. The tax authority may obtain personal asset preservation orders, impose exit controls until the tax is settled, and pursue criminal charges for tax evasion where the directors intentionally concealed the non-resident dividend to defraud the State, with a maximum imprisonment of seven years.
